description: The Day filter on Find a Circle now opens on top of everything else instead of sliding behind the Status and ACPD filters below it. On phones the list was effectively unusable — days at the bottom were covered up and couldn't be tapped. The menu now stays anchored to the field as you scroll, flips above the field when there isn't room below, keeps itself inside the screen edges, and scrolls internally when space is tight. You can also close it with Escape or by tapping away.

Three more accuracy holes closed. People removed from a circle in CCB now actually leave the RADIUS roster: every roster refresh compares the fresh CCB member list against what's cached and deactivates anyone who's gone, so departed members stop appearing on roster pages, in member counts, and in coaching automations. (They're deactivated rather than deleted — if a bad CCB response ever drops someone by mistake, the next good refresh brings them right back, and an empty response never wipes a roster.) Meeting reminders now refuse to run on old calendar data: if a circle's cached CCB calendar hasn't been refreshed in three days, its reminders pause instead of nudging leaders about times the church may have changed, and the gap is logged so it's findable. And the dashboard's Needs Attention sync endpoint now requires a signed-in session — it could previously be triggered by anyone, spending CCB API quota and rewriting attendance records without authentication.

Syncing a circle from CCB now reads the circle's current calendar event instead of whichever event CCB happened to list first. A circle's CCB calendar keeps its whole history — when a circle changed its meeting day or time, the old event stayed in the list, and both "Re-sync from CCB" and the importer kept reading the retired schedule as if it were current. The sync now ranks the group's events and takes the one actually in effect today: an active repeating series wins over one-off gatherings and over events whose run has ended, and a brand-new schedule beats the one it replaced. On top of that, every CCB read now goes out with caching explicitly disabled, so a sync can never be answered from a saved copy of an old CCB response — what you see in a sync preview is what CCB has right now.

A sweep of the attendance and event-summary pipeline closed several ways old or empty CCB records could replace real ones. The nightly attendance sync compared CCB's records against expected meeting dates using mismatched date formats, so it filled "no record" stubs over meetings that actually had attendance — a summary a leader submitted could vanish overnight. That comparison is fixed, and CCB deep links that rendered as "Invalid DateTime" now point at the right occurrence. When CCB holds both a pre-created empty attendance record and the one a leader actually filled in for the same week, the filled-in one now wins instead of whichever CCB listed first, so circles stop reading as "nothing received" when a summary exists. A circle's saved CCB event list can no longer be wiped by one failed lookup, attendance found on a profile page only files under a leader when the event title actually names them (a similarly-named circle's meetings no longer land on the wrong leader or overwrite their match key), roster contact info now prefers what CCB just returned over an older saved copy, and a failed overnight cache refresh keeps yesterday's good attendance data instead of erasing it.

Mass Update now has Sync from CCB: select any set of circles and refresh their data straight from CCB in one run. It works in two steps so nothing is written blind — Check pulls each selected circle fresh from CCB in small paced batches (gentle on CCB's API limits, with live progress and a Stop button) and lays out exactly which fields would change, from and to; Apply then writes only the changes you keep ticked. Circles that are already accurate say so, and problem circles are flagged instead of silently skipped — no CCB Group ID on file, group not found in CCB, or group marked inactive in CCB. Leader names stay untouched unless you opt in, so couple-led circles keep their combined RADIUS name. It updates the same fields as the per-circle "Re-sync from CCB": meeting day, time, frequency, location, campus, circle type, leader contact info and birthday, CCB group name, and linked event IDs.

Adding someone to a bulk message by searching CCB now picks up their birthday, so the under-18 check actually applies to them. Their details arrive from CCB in two steps — the search result first, then the full profile a moment later — and the second step was being discarded as a duplicate, which left everyone added this way looking like their age was unknown. A minor added by hand could still be texted. The same fix keeps CCB's better phone number when the profile has one, instead of adding the person to the list a second time.

Adding a circle's roster to a bulk message can now pull from CCB's newer API, which returns everyone's phone number and birthday in a single call. The old path asked CCB for one person at a time and ran out of time on Netlify at around eighteen people, and it only ever learned a birthday for someone whose phone number was missing — so most rosters came in with no ages to check against. If the newer API is unavailable the roster still loads the old way rather than failing, and inactive members stay excluded either way. Turning this on is a setting change; nothing about the roster looks different when it's off.

Anyone under 18 is now held back from bulk texting. On Bulk Message and on a campaign's Follow Up, people who can't be texted move to their own "Can't send" list that names each person and the reason — "Under 18" with their age, or "No phone". They're skipped by the step-through batch, by Auto Send, and by the per-person Send button, and they're never marked contacted, so they stay on your list to follow up another way. Ages come from a leader's birthday in RADIUS, a birthdate CCB has on file, or a Birthdate or Age column on a pasted roster or list. When someone has no birthdate on record the check can't run for them, and the page says so instead of implying the whole list was verified — a campaign's CSV export now carries Age and Can Text columns so you can see the coverage yourself.

Find a Circle now shows each leader's phone number in the results table, so you can call or text a leader straight from the list instead of opening their profile first. Numbers are formatted for readability and tap-to-call on mobile. The column is only visible when you're signed in -- public visitors browsing for a circle still don't see leader phone numbers.

Leaders missing a phone number can now be filled in from CCB without leaving Bulk Message. Where the recipients panel lists who can't be texted, a Fill from CCB button looks each one up and saves any number CCB has, then refreshes the list so they join the recipients immediately. Anyone CCB has no number for is named separately from anyone who couldn't be matched to a CCB profile at all — so what's left is a real worklist rather than a guess. It only ever fills blanks, never overwriting a number already in Radius, so it's safe to re-run. Lookups go to CCB in small batches with a pause between each, and if CCB's daily read budget runs out it says how many were saved before it stopped.

Circles already holding a wrong location can now be repaired in bulk instead of one re-sync at a time. An admin-only backfill re-reads every circle's location from its CCB group address, previews exactly what would change before anything is written, and skips circles whose CCB group has no address on file so a blank in CCB can never wipe a location in RADIUS.

Circle locations now come from the address on the group's "When & Where" tab in CCB, which is the field you actually edit. Previously RADIUS read the address off the group's calendar event instead — and CCB only copies the address onto an event when that event is created, so any circle that changed venue kept showing its old meeting spot no matter how many times you re-synced. Venue names also stopped getting shortened: a group whose street reads "Einstein Bros. Bagels" no longer comes through as just "Einstein Bros", and a multi-line address is tidied onto one line. Re-sync any circle whose location looks wrong to pull the corrected value.

Bulk Message now explains why the recipient count is smaller than the number of leaders your filters matched. Filtering by an ACPD could match 75 leaders and produce 33 recipients with nothing to explain the gap — leaders with no phone number on file can't be texted, and anyone sharing a number with someone already on the list is skipped so they don't get the same message twice. A line above the recipients now reads how many matched and how many were left out, split by reason, and Show lists them by name and campus with a link straight to each profile. That doubles as a to-do list: fill in a missing phone number and the leader joins the next list automatically.

An additional leader can now be edited or removed from a circle's profile. Until now the additional leader's name showed next to the circle name in the header, on dashboard cards, and in search results, but there was nowhere to change it — so when someone stepped down, their name stayed. The profile now has an Additional Leader card holding their name, phone, email, birthday, and CCB profile link, with the same Fill from CCB search the primary leader has. Hit Edit and the card gains a Remove button that clears all five fields at once, so the person also drops out of bulk messaging, the prayer list, and the birthday list rather than lingering with a leftover phone number. Save to apply, or Cancel to back out. The card appears once someone is set, and while editing so one can be added.

The export on Find a Circle can now include each circle's location. Location joins the Include fields checkboxes — checked by default, and you can uncheck it like any other field — and it carries through all three outputs: copy to clipboard, the text file, and the CSV. Circles with no location recorded read "Not specified" in the text export and come through as an empty cell in the CSV, so the column still lines up in a spreadsheet.

The CCB-calendar-as-schedule feature from August 6 is backed out for now. In practice the calendar sync kept colliding with CCB's per-endpoint rate limits, leaving most circles stuck in "Sync failed" states and their schedules locked read-only — so everything returns to how it worked before: day, time, and frequency are hand-editable everywhere again (profile, mass update, row edit), the event summary tracker, daily digest, and Today read those fields directly, and the Calendar Sync tab is gone. Nothing was lost: snapshots that did sync stay stored in the database, and circles whose schedule was filled in from their calendar keep those values — now editable if any look wrong. The feature will come back once the sync is redesigned to live within CCB's limits.

The calendar backfill kept tripping CCB's per-endpoint rate limit: after the first few circles, CCB answered every request with "rate limited (429), retry after 1s" — and RADIUS treated each of those as a hard failure, so one busy stretch cascaded into a whole run of failed circles. RADIUS now does exactly what CCB's reply asks: it waits the second or two and quietly retries (up to a few attempts), so bulk syncs pace themselves instead of collapsing. Genuine limit problems — a long cool-down or persistent throttling — still surface as errors. Bulk runs take a little longer now; that's the rate limit being respected rather than fought.

The Calendar Sync backfill could die mid-run: a batch with several slow-failing circles ran past the server's time limit, got killed, and the page then crashed on the dead response (on iPad that surfaced as Safari's cryptic "The string did not match the expected pattern") — abandoning every circle it hadn't reached yet. The server now stops before its time limit and hands unfinished circles back, the page automatically re-queues them and keeps going, and a batch that dies outright is reported without ending the run. The Status column also now shows the actual reason under each "Sync failed" badge, so a failing circle explains itself right in the table.

Resync Calendar on a circle's profile (and the Import Circles calendar backfill) could fail with an unexplained "HTTP 412" from CCB. The sync asks CCB for the circle's full schedule window — eight weeks back through a year ahead — in a single request, and CCB can refuse a request that wide. When that happens, RADIUS now automatically retries in narrower date slices until CCB accepts, stitches the results back together, and carries on; nothing changes about what gets synced. And if CCB turns a sync down for any other reason, the error message now includes CCB's own explanation instead of just a bare status code, so it's clear what to fix.

A circle's meeting schedule now comes straight from its CCB group calendar instead of hand-kept day/time/frequency fields. Importing a circle snapshots the calendar's actual event dates (a year ahead) into RADIUS, derives the day, time, and frequency from them — including odd cadences like "1st, 3rd" that CCB's recurrence codes couldn't express — and every schedule surface reads those real dates: the event summary tracker, circle reporting, the daily digest, Today, and attendance sync (which no longer invents "no record" weeks for ordinal circles). Schedule fields on calendar-synced circles are read-only; change the events in CCB, then hit Resync Calendar on the profile. Syncs are deliberately manual — a new Calendar Sync tab on Import Circles backfills or refreshes everyone in batches. If a circle's calendar has no upcoming dates, RADIUS flags it on the profile and the tracker with instructions (set up the recurring event in CCB, then resync) and falls back to the last known schedule so the circle never disappears.

Pulling a CCB group roster could time out and fail with a bare 502 instead of returning anyone. CCB's group data often leaves phone numbers out, so RADIUS was fetching them one person at a time — which takes half a second each and runs past the server's ten-second limit at around eighteen people, smaller than most real groups. Callers can now ask for the roster without the phone numbers and get it back in about a second, then fill the numbers in afterwards through a new endpoint that works in timed batches and hands back whatever it didn't reach. RADIUS's own screens are unchanged — they still get phone numbers the way they always have.

When you paste a list into a campaign, a cell holding several values separated by semicolons — "Hosts; Prayer" in a Team column — was read as a single value, so that person ended up on one team literally named "Hosts; Prayer" instead of showing up under both. It now splits into separate values, so grouping and filtering find them under each one. Commas are deliberately left alone, since campus names contain them ("Flower Mound, North"). This also makes duplicating a pasted-list campaign exact: someone on two teams with no CCB ID used to come back merged into that junk value.

RADIUS can now hand Valley Creek Pulse a CCB form's responses, which is what lets Pulse run its own follow-up campaigns. Pulse holds no CCB credentials of its own — every CCB call it makes comes through RADIUS, so the church's shared 10,000-a-day CCB limit still has exactly one consumer, with one budget guard and one set of telemetry watching it. The existing group roster endpoint can also return the group's name now when asked, so Pulse can roll a campaign up by campus without anyone re-typing group names. Nothing changes for RADIUS itself: campaigns here work exactly as they did.

"Re-sync from CCB" on a leader's profile was proposing changes that were wrong every single time, and it turned out to be three separate problems. Circle Type was being read from the wrong place in CCB -- it was pulling CCB's own group category ("Small Group") instead of the Circle Type field your team fills in, so every re-sync offered to overwrite Men's or YA | Co-Ed with something meaningless. Values that were already correct were being flagged as changes because they were merely spelled differently: a circle stored as "7:00 PM" looked different from CCB's "19:00", "1st & 3rd" looked different from "1st, 3rd", and "Bi-Weekly" looked different from "Bi-weekly" -- so a re-sync could never come back clean, and accepting one left the circle in a format the profile dropdowns couldn't match. And it was all-or-nothing: one bad row meant cancelling the whole thing, so genuinely useful updates like a new meeting time or a missing phone number couldn't be taken on their own. Circle Type now comes from the right field, matching values are recognised as matching and left alone, whatever you do accept is saved in RADIUS's own format, and every change has its own tick box so you can take the good ones and leave the rest -- handy for circles led by a couple, where CCB only knows one of the two names.

You can add a leader by hand again, on a new Add a Leader page. Importing from CCB had become the only way in, which left no room for an invited leader, someone in the pipeline, a circle with no CCB group, or a team with no scheduling category. Start by searching CCB for the person -- their name, email, phone and birthday come straight across, and their profile link is recorded for you -- or skip the search and type everything yourself. Then pick whether you're adding a Circle Leader or a Team Leader and the form follows: a circle asks for its circle name, meeting day, time, frequency and circle type with an ACPD as its director, while a team asks for its team name with a director from the team directors list. Name is the only thing required; everything else can wait until later on the leader's profile. Bi-weekly circles get their start date field, and if the circle or team already exists in CCB you can record its group or category ID. Type a name that's already in RADIUS and you'll get a heads-up before you create a duplicate. Once saved, the leader opens straight to their profile. You'll find it in the sidebar under Admin Tools, as an "Add Leader" button on Find a Circle, and linked from both import pages.

Looking a leader up on Import Host Team now brings their birthday over too, alongside the name, email and phone it already filled in. CCB's search results don't carry birthdays -- only the full profile does -- so the birthday was quietly being left behind and had to be added by hand later. There's a Birthday field on the form now, filled in for you when you use the lookup and editable if CCB has it wrong or missing. If CCB is slow or unreachable on that second step, the contact details still come across and you're told the birthday didn't.

Marking circles active or inactive in CCB from Mass Update failed for every circle, reporting "Request failed with status code 500" next to each leader's name. RADIUS was sending CCB the change to make but not the circle it applied to, so CCB had nothing to update and rejected the whole write. The circle is now identified the way CCB expects, and the update goes through. RADIUS also reads CCB's reply back to confirm each circle actually landed on the value you picked, and when CCB does reject something it now reports what CCB said instead of a bare error code.

Marking circles active or inactive in CCB from Mass Update failed with a server timeout when more than a couple of circles were selected. Each circle is a separate call out to CCB, and the whole selection was being sent as one request that ran past the time limit -- so the update died with no report, even though some circles had already been changed. Mass Update now sends circles to CCB in small batches, shows its progress as it works through them, and if a batch does fail it tells you exactly how many were updated before it stopped. Re-running is safe: circles already set to the value you picked are left alone.

You can now mark circles active or inactive in Church Community Builder straight from Mass Update. Pick "CCB Circle Status" under the new CCB group in the Field to Update list, choose Active or Inactive, select your leaders, and confirm -- RADIUS updates each circle's group in CCB for you, instead of you opening CCB and editing them one at a time. This one writes to CCB rather than RADIUS, so it's marked in amber and asks you to confirm before it runs, and a leader's RADIUS status is left exactly as it was. Leaders with no CCB circle linked are named up front and skipped, and anything CCB rejects is listed by name afterward so nothing fails quietly.

Submitting a Circle Summary more than once no longer inflates the attendance number in Church Community Builder. Guests you add by hand (people who aren't on your roster) are sent to CCB as a head count, and CCB *adds* that number to the meeting instead of replacing it -- so a resubmission, or an automatic retry after a network hiccup, silently counted those guests a second time. Three walk-ins could end up in CCB as six or nine, while the attendee list and notes looked perfectly correct. The toolkit now reads what CCB already has for that meeting and sends only the difference, so submitting again changes nothing. Roster attendees were never affected -- CCB matches those to real people. If CCB is already carrying more guests than your summary reports, it's flagged for the office to correct, because a head count in CCB can be added to but never lowered through the API.

The Connection Tracker now always reads live circle data. It had been serving a frozen snapshot of the leader list, so renamed leaders kept their old names (circle 597 still read "Cindy Cross" after it became "Deborah Weeger"), newly created circles never appeared at all, and every leader's status stayed stuck at whatever it was when the snapshot was taken. Names, statuses, and new circles now show up as soon as they're saved. Logged connections on a leader's page get the same fix.

The status filter on the Connection Tracker now lists every leader status -- Invited, Pipeline, On-Boarding, Active, Paused, and Off-Boarding -- instead of only the statuses leaders happen to have right now. Previously the dropdown was built from whoever was on the page, so in a season where every leader is paused, Paused was the only choice and you couldn't filter down to your active leaders.

Meetings your Circle actually held now always show up in the Events list, even when they fall outside your usual meeting rhythm. Previously, if a bi-weekly Circle met on an off week, that meeting was hidden from the toolkit (and couldn't be summarized) because it didn't match the expected schedule -- even though attendance was already recorded in Church Community Builder. Now any date with recorded attendance or a submitted summary is shown regardless of cadence, while blank off-week dates stay hidden so the list doesn't fill up with meetings that never happened.

Circle leader profiles now include a Circle Snapshot (ACPD only): pick a timeframe -- last month, 3 months, 6 months, or this semester -- and instantly see the honest numbers for that circle: average attendance and whether it's trending up or down, what percentage of the roster shows up, meetings met vs. skipped, who was added to the roster, new faces and when they first appeared, and who's been showing up consistently. From there, one tap generates an AI coaching summary that reads the whole timeframe's meeting notes and gives you a coaching read: themes in the notes, what to celebrate, what to watch for, and suggested questions for your next conversation. Generated summaries are saved and shared, so other ACPDs see them without re-generating.

Auto Send now has its own home in Settings. The new Auto Send tab checks everything in one place: whether the Mac Companion server is running and up to date, whether the Messages app is ready to send, whether Text Message Forwarding can reach non-iPhone numbers, and whether delivery tracking (Full Disk Access) is on. You can run all the checks with one click, walk through the guided setup, and send yourself a test text that confirms the whole pipeline -- including the delivery receipt. The setup prompts on Bulk Message and Campaigns now point here instead of each carrying their own copy of the wizard.

Deleting a board, list, card, label, or checklist now shows Radius's own confirmation dialog instead of the browser's built-in popup. In some embedded browsers those built-in popups never appeared, which made delete buttons look broken -- clicking Delete did nothing. The new dialog always shows up, matches the app's dark styling, and supports Enter to confirm and Escape to cancel.

Boards can now import people straight from a CCB event. Open the board menu, choose Import from CCB Event, and enter the event's ID -- everyone who checked in is pulled up, one card per person. Want just the newcomers? Add an optional created-after date and only attendees whose CCB profile was created after that date are included. Each card's title is the person's name, and the description includes the event they attended (with the day they showed up), their phone and email (so the Call, Text, and Email buttons work right away), and when their profile was created. Before importing you choose which list the cards land on and can tag them all with an existing label or create a new one on the spot.

The Mass Update tool's Status dropdown now lists every leader status, including Pipeline and Archived. Previously it only offered a fixed subset, so you couldn't mass-archive circles or move a batch of leaders into the Pipeline status.

The Circle Summary submit button now shows a radiating circle animation while your submission is being sent. The expanding circles give visual feedback that something is happening and reinforce the app's identity.

Submitting a Circle Summary now double-checks that it actually landed in Church Community Builder before showing success. Previously, CCB could occasionally accept a submission and quietly drop it -- the toolkit said it worked, but the summary never appeared in CCB. Now the toolkit reads the summary back from CCB right after saving; if it isn't there, it automatically saves it a second time, and if CCB still doesn't have it you'll see a clear message asking you to tap Submit Again -- with everything you typed kept in place, so nothing needs to be re-entered. Connection drops get the same treatment: your answers stay put and the button simply becomes Submit Again.

The Circles Toolkit is quicker to open and move around in. Tapping Submit on a summary no longer waits on an extra Church Community Builder lookup it never used, the Roster tab stops re-downloading the list it just showed you, and switching back to the app from another app no longer re-runs the whole alert check every time. The red needs summary dot on the Events tab is now counted from data already on hand instead of a fresh CCB call, so it can lag by a few minutes in one specific case: a summary entered directly in CCB rather than in the toolkit. Summaries submitted in the toolkit still clear it instantly, and opening the Events tab always shows the live, authoritative list. Separately, actions like saving a draft, searching for a member, or submitting a summary were each quietly making two trips to the server instead of one -- now they make one.

The Status and ACPD filters on Find a Circle now let you pick more than one at a time. Check off any combination -- Active and Paused, or two ACPDs -- and each one shows as a removable chip in the field. Pick All Statuses or All ACPDs to clear them.

Text or call a person straight from their card on a campaign. The Text button opens Messages with the campaign message already filled in for them -- the same one-tap outreach as a leader's profile page -- and after you send, a one-tap Mark contacted logs it without opening the bulk Follow Up flow.
